title: Scheduling and Quota Resume command contracts
$comment: Owner contract schema named by Plans/Commands_System.md (Puppet Master Assistant Redesign Central Registration Addendum - 2026-09-03: "Naming them here does not create them") for Plans/Scheduling_and_Quota_Resume.md. Written 2026-09-27 as the companion of ledger pldg-20260927-003-wand-scheduling (register line B-SQR-09; SQR-013, SQR-015, SQR-017): the request/result pairs of the six commands the wand-module scheduling surfaces dispatch, cmd.chat.schedule_message, cmd.chat.schedule_message.update, cmd.chat.schedule_message.cancel, cmd.chat.plan.schedule_build, cmd.execution_window.update and cmd.execution_window.cancel. Closure wave 2026-09-27 (register line B-SQR-05, card p12, DL-136; SQR-018, CS-087, UCC-174): AutomationPauseSetRequest/Result for cmd.runtime.automation_pause.set, with ProjectAutomationPauseRecord, the shape of the project-scoped pause record SQR-018 owns (its storage key and storage-registry entry are not made here). cmd.runtime.automation_stop.set is not an identity and has no definition. ExecutionWindowCreateRequest/Result (cmd.execution_window.create) and QuotaResumeConsentRequest/Result (cmd.runtime.quota_resume.set) are intentionally absent and remain future owner-authored additions to this file, so those rows keep handler_unavailable truthfully. The payload of runtime.automation_pause_changed and the failed clause project_automation_paused on scheduled_dispatch.held and runtime.quota_resume_attempted wait on central EventRecord registration with the other twelve scheduling events and are not defined here. The stored records pm.chat.scheduled_message_snapshot.v1 and pm.execution.schedule.v1 are not redefined: the latter lives in Plans/assistant_plan_cancel_custody.schema.json, which does not yet carry grace_seconds (ledger question q-004). A definition here is a contract shape, not a handler, a catalogue registration or an admission: every command stays handler_unavailable. Requests and results are not records and add no storage key, EventRecord, writer or physical family.

iana_timezone.description: An IANA zone name, never a fixed offset (section 3, Execution windows). UTC is a valid choice but is never the sheet's default (SQR-017); the default is a surface rule, not a shape.

missed_policy.description: Stored missed-time policy (section 3). Surfaces label these values per SQR-017 and never rename them.

grace_seconds.description: The grace recorded for cancel_after_grace. The sheets show whole minutes and record exactly the shown value in seconds (SQR-015, SQR-017), so it is a positive multiple of 60.

schedule_command_error_code.description: The closed typed-error set of Plans/Scheduling_and_Quota_Resume.md section 3 (Exact commands and required result boundaries). A failure never returns a success-shaped result and never advances a schedule.

scheduled_send_time.description: A concrete send time: the owner's UTC instant plus the IANA zone and local wall time the user chose, validated as future in that zone before admission (SQR-010).

missed_policy_with_grace.description: grace_seconds is a recorded value exactly when the policy is cancel_after_grace, and null otherwise (a value the sheet does not show is not recorded).

execution_window_spec.description: The window specification a Build At commit carries inside AssistantPlanScheduleRequest (SQR-013, REV-9) and an edit carries inside ExecutionWindowUpdateRequest. Field names follow pm.execution.schedule.v1 (section 3, Execution windows); local_start_date and grace_seconds are request-side fields that record exactly what the Build At sheet shows (SQR-015). one_time names a date and no weekdays; recurring_window names at least one weekday (1 = Monday .. 7 = Sunday) and no date.

scheduled_message_changes.description: The edited fields of a scheduled or held message. Every present field replaces the frozen value in a new snapshot revision; an absent field keeps it. text keeps the schedule_text_not_empty rule.

schedule_text.description: The Schedule Message sheet's own text (precondition schedule_text_not_empty, SQR-013): at least one non-whitespace character. An empty composer does not matter; empty sheet text is refused invalid_request.

ScheduledMessageCreateRequest.description: ScheduledMessageCreateRequest for cmd.chat.schedule_message (SQR-002, SQR-013; Commands_System.md central registration). The only GUI producer is the schedule_sheet primary; the wand row only opens the sheet. The text is the sheet's own editable text, prefilled from the composer; text_from_composer says whether the committed text is the composer's, and composer_buffer_ref names that buffer so the owner clears it only after the durable commit and only in that case. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

ScheduledMessageCreateResult.description: ScheduledMessageCreateResult. An accepted commit returns the scheduled_dispatch_id and frozen snapshot ref at revision 1 in state scheduled, and only then may the card render (SMSG-001). A rejection names its typed reason, creates nothing and leaves the composer untouched (composer_cleared false). Creates no Goal, Plan or To-Do.

ScheduledMessageUpdateRequest.description: ScheduledMessageUpdateRequest for cmd.chat.schedule_message.update: Edit (changes), Reschedule (reschedule_to a new time), Edit and send (changes plus reschedule_to "now") and Send now on a held message, including a missed one (reschedule_to "now" and no changes). There is no separate send-now command (SQR-013, CDRY-008). Under the expected revision and currentness; refused dispatch_already_started once dispatch has started, and never applied to a dispatched message. Surfaces are the existing schedule_details plus scheduled_message_card and schedule_manager (UCC-169). A request that changes nothing is invalid.

ScheduledMessageUpdateResult.description: ScheduledMessageUpdateResult. An accepted update rebinds the exact snapshot as a new revision of the same scheduled_dispatch_id (no second schedule, SQR-010) in state scheduled; with reschedule_to now, scheduled_at_utc is the owner's server time and the internal scheduler dispatch follows in its own idempotency domain. A rejected update reports the unchanged record: its revision, state, snapshot and time stay as they were, and a prior failed attempt is never overwritten (SMSG-013).

ScheduledMessageCancelRequest.description: ScheduledMessageCancelRequest for cmd.chat.schedule_message.cancel, with the expected revision and currentness (SQR-013). Cancels exactly one schedule; siblings in the thread are untouched (SMSG-012, SMSG-016).

ScheduledMessageCancelResult.description: ScheduledMessageCancelResult. Accepted is terminal cancelled; the snapshot is retained for audit on every path and is never dispatched.

AssistantPlanScheduleRequest.description: AssistantPlanScheduleRequest for cmd.chat.plan.schedule_build. One Build At commit is this one command: the window specification rides inside the request, and the owner creates the exact-version binding and its ExecutionSchedule in one transaction, never paired with cmd.execution_window.create (SQR-013, REV-9). expected_revision is the Plan's revision at the sheet. Exactly one execution_topology is frozen; crew carries the validated CollaborationDefinition ref and the others carry none (PSCHED-001..003). Use V<n> on the Plan card is this command against the new version's exact hash with reschedule_of_schedule_id naming the invalidated schedule, which stays invalidated as its audit record. Sources: plan_schedule (the Build At sheet) and plan_card (Use V<n>).

ExecutionScheduleResult.description: ExecutionScheduleResult. Accepted returns the schedule_id (the id Cancel schedule later targets) and the binding ref together, at revision 1 and state active, with the recorded window echoed value for value, so the sheet can read back exactly what it showed (SQR-015). Rejected returns neither: no half-created schedule exists. Neither path admits a run: no PlanRun, Goal, CrewRun, work binding or provider attempt exists before first eligible dispatch (PSCHED-001..003, PGOAL-015).

ExecutionWindowUpdateRequest.description: ExecutionWindowUpdateRequest for cmd.execution_window.update: editing a build schedule (SQR-013) under the expected revision, refused once dispatch has started. The exact target binding does not change here; a new Plan version is Use V<n>, not an edit. Surfaces are the registered plan_schedule, run_schedule and settings plus schedule_manager (UCC-169).

ExecutionWindowUpdateResult.description: ExecutionWindowUpdateResult. The same schedule_id at a new revision with the recorded window echoed; an in-flight run's admission never changes silently, and a narrowed window takes effect at the next wind-down boundary. A rejected update echoes the unchanged record.

ExecutionWindowCancelRequest.description: ExecutionWindowCancelRequest for cmd.execution_window.cancel, including Cancel schedule, which targets the schedule_id cmd.chat.plan.schedule_build returned; there is no schedule_build.cancel (SQR-013). Surfaces are the registered plan_schedule, run_schedule and settings, schedule_manager (UCC-169), and plan_card for Cancel schedule on the Plan card's Schedule needs update line (SQR-013, SQR-015; plan_card is a registered source surface of the scheduling family).

ExecutionWindowCancelResult.description: ExecutionWindowCancelResult. Accepted is terminal cancelled. Work already admitted continues under its own owner: cancelling a window is not a Stop, so admitted_work_stopped is false on every path.

automation_pause_actor_kind.description: Who originated the dispatch. Only user is ever accepted (SQR-018, DL-136; CS-087): an assistant or agent tool call, the scheduler, an execution window, a quota resume, Crew Auto, Goal or Plan continuation (automation) and system are all refused with permission_denied. Every non-user kind is listed so that a refused dispatch has a well-formed request to refuse.

ProjectAutomationPauseRecord.description: The project-scoped operational record behind "Pause all automations" (SQR-018): owned by Plans/Scheduling_and_Quota_Resume.md and never a Settings value; no Settings default seeds it. One record per project. user_stop_epoch is the project's monotonically increasing epoch that every eligibility evaluation for a target in the project captures beside the target's own (section 1; SQR-006, clause project_automation_paused). Only a user ever changes the record, so changed_by_actor_kind is user or, while the record is still at its initial revision 0 (switch off, never changed), null. A paused record always names the user who paused it and when ("Paused by you at <time>"). Contract shape only: its storage key and storage-registry entry are not made here (ledger question q-006).

automation_pause_side_effects.description: What the switch never does (SQR-018): turning it on cancels nothing, invalidates no schedule and disables no quota consent; neither direction changes a per-run manual Pause, Stop or Cancel latch; and the command dispatches nothing by itself (turning it off only lets the one predicate evaluate held items again). Every member is false on every path.

AutomationPauseSetRequest.description: AutomationPauseSetRequest for cmd.runtime.automation_pause.set (SQR-018, DL-136; CS-087, UCC-174). Project-scoped: the target identity is the envelope's project_id and there is no other target. paused true turns "Pause all automations" on and latches a manual stop at project scope by advancing the project's user_stop_epoch the way Manual Stop does; paused false ("Turn back on", or the switch itself) is the only clear. The only source surface is schedule_manager (the Resume & Safety Policy tab), never settings: the switch is not a Settings value. The command sets an absolute value and is idempotent by value (a request that sets the value the switch already has returns the record unchanged and does not advance the epoch again), so it carries no expected_revision. actor_kind records who originated the dispatch; the owner accepts only user and refuses every other kind with permission_denied, and no automatic producer dispatches it. There is no toggle, inherit or automation_stop spelling. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

AutomationPauseSetResult.description: AutomationPauseSetResult. Every path returns the project's pause record (paused, the project's user_stop_epoch, who changed it, when, and its revision). Accepted: the record holds the requested value; changed is true only when the value moved, and then the owner emits runtime.automation_pause_changed once (section 3, Events; its EventRecord is not registered yet, so no event type is claimed here). Only a change to paused true advances the epoch; an idempotent re-set (changed false) and turning the switch off never do. Rejected (for example permission_denied for a non-user actor, which is how an automatic clear is refused) changes nothing and echoes the unchanged record. The side_effects members are false on every path.
